about: Chicago Trade License Finder data (tools/dp_licenses.py). Every line read on its agency page on the checked date; Todd's go Oct 27, 2026 (coo/PARALLEL_BUILDS.md).
lede: What the City of Chicago and the State of Illinois require for 12 trades, from fee and insurance to bond, exam and renewal, each line linked to the agency page.
method: We read every line on the issuing agency's own page: the City of Chicago Departments of Buildings, Business Affairs and Consumer Protection, Public Health and Transportation; the Illinois Departments of Public Health, Agriculture, and Financial and Professional Regulation; Illinois EPA; State law on the Illinois General Assembly site; and the U.S. EPA. Each line links to its page and the date we read it.
Where an agency page is silent, the line says so, such as not stated or lists no bond, instead of filling the gap. A page we could not open is not used.

For trades the City pages we read do not name, such as cleaning, painting, pest control, landscaping, pressure washing and snow removal, the page reports what BACP says about how it picks a license and the fee in its license table, not a guess at which license applies.

When this page's data changes, a checker re-reads the source pages it can reach and flags any figure that is no longer printed there. This is public information, not legal advice; the agency decides what your business needs.
faq: Does a license from a suburb count in Chicago?

None of the City pages we read says a suburb's license counts in Chicago. For plumbing, the City says a State registered contractor also needs a City plumbing contractor license. Roofers hold one State license, and a Chicago roof permit still needs a City licensed general contractor.
Which general contractor class do I need?

The Department of Buildings sets the class by the largest single project value and the demolition allowed: Class E up to $500,000 with no demolition, D up to $2 million and C up to $5 million with ordinary demolition, B up to $10 million and A with no limit, both with ordinary or complex demolition. The picker on this page gives the smallest class that covers both.
Does Chicago have an HVAC license?

No City page we read names a separate HVAC license. Permitted HVAC work needs a City general contractor license, Class A to E, and home heating and cooling work without a permit falls under the City home repair license. Refrigerant work needs EPA Section 608 certification.
Does the surface cleaning permit cover pressure washing?
The Chicago Department of Public Health permit names sandblasting, grinding and chemical washing. The City pages we read do not mention power or pressure washing.

Every line was read on its agency page on Oct 27, 2026, and each shows that date. Fees and rules change. BACP has posted a business license fee update dated Jan 27, 2026 that we could not open, so the City business license fees shown here may be out of date.

trades.name: General contractor
trades.title: Chicago General Contractor License: Classes and Fees
trades.desc: Chicago general contractor license classes A to E: project limits, demolition, insurance, fees and renewal, from the Department of Buildings page.
trades.card: Classes A to E, $300 to $2,000 a year
trades.summary: One City license in five classes, set by your largest single project and the demolition you do. We found no State general contractor license on the State pages we read.
trades.page_summary: The City of Chicago licenses general contractors in five classes, A to E, set by the largest single project value and the demolition allowed. Here is each class, its fee and insurance, and what the State adds.

rows.text: The Department of Buildings requires a general contractor license for most building construction, alteration, repair and demolition work in Chicago. Licensed plumbing, electrical and mason contractors working within their own license, and subcontractors working under a licensed general contractor, do not need one.

Five classes: A has no project limit, B goes to $10 million, C to $5 million, D to $2 million and E to $500,000 for the largest single project. A and B may do ordinary or complex demolition, C and D ordinary only, E none.

An individual working on their own primary residence needs no general contractor license if the building has three or fewer stories above grade, six or fewer dwelling units and no nonresidential use. Excavation and demolition still need one. Only one property a calendar year qualifies.

The State's professional regulation list has no general contractor license, and roofing is the only construction trade on that list. No State agency page we read says the State licenses general contractors.
The City says licenses issued by the State of Illinois may also be needed for some kinds of construction, demolition, repair and maintenance work.
License and yearly renewal: Class A $2,000, Class B $1,000, Class C $750, Class D $500, Class E $300.

Class A $5 million and Class B $3 million per occurrence (primary or umbrella); Classes C and D $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate; Class E $1 million per occurrence. The insurer must be rated B+ or better, and the license goes inactive if the policy lapses.

State law: a business doing home repair and remodeling carries liability insurance of $100,000 per person and $300,000 per occurrence for bodily injury and $50,000 per occurrence for property damage, plus $10,000 per occurrence for work not done to code, unless its net worth is at least $1,000,000.
The City page lists no bond.

The City page lists no exam. Continental Testing Services takes applications by mail for the Department of Buildings, with a statement of financial solvency, proof of insurance, proof of authority to do business in Illinois (not for sole proprietors) and photo ID.
A license is valid for one year from issuance. Renewal goes to Continental Testing Services by mail with proof of current insurance.
Not stated. The City page does not say whether a license from a suburb or another town counts in Chicago.
Firms whose work disturbs lead-based paint in homes, child care facilities and kindergartens built before 1978 must be certified by EPA or an authorized state and use certified renovators.

glance: General contractor license, Class A to E
None found

rows.text: The Department of Buildings requires an electrical contractor license to install, alter or maintain wiring or equipment covered by the Chicago Electrical Code. It comes in two types: General and Low Voltage.

Supervising electrician: $150 per exam, $150 for the license and $150 a year to renew.
The City electrical contractor page lists no insurance amount.
The City electrical contractor page lists no bond.
Continental Testing Services gives the supervising electrician written exams for the Department of Buildings.
The contractor license type, General or Low Voltage, follows the exam the business's licensed supervising electrician passed.
The contractor license runs one year and renews through the Department of Buildings web portal.
Not stated. The City electrical pages do not say whether a license from a suburb or another town counts in Chicago.

trades.name: Plumbing
trades.title: Chicago Plumbing License: City and State Rules
trades.desc: What Chicago and Illinois require of plumbers and plumbing contractors: licenses, fees, $20,000 bonds, insurance, exams and renewal, from agency pages.
trades.card: City license plus State registration, $20,000 bonds
trades.summary: Both the City and the State license plumbing. A State registered contractor still needs a City plumbing contractor license to work in Chicago.
trades.page_summary: Plumbing is licensed by both the City of Chicago and the Illinois Department of Public Health. Here is what each requires of contractors and plumbers, and how the two fit together.

rows.text: The Department of Buildings requires a plumbing contractor license to install, alter, repair or maintain plumbing piping. Only a plumber licensed by the City can file the application.
Plumbers need a City plumber license, and a plumber license from the Illinois Department of Public Health is also valid in Chicago when the employer holds a City plumbing contractor license.
The Illinois Department of Public Health licenses plumbers and apprentices, and every plumbing contractor registers with the State and pays a yearly fee.
For State registration, the owner, a partner, or a named officer, member or manager is the licensed plumber of record, and one plumber can be plumber of record for only one company.
City plumbing contractor: $150 to start and $150 a year to renew.
City plumber: $150 for the license and $150 a year to renew. The exam is $175 for current City or State licensed apprentices and $225 for everyone else.
State plumbing contractor registration: $150 a year.

State registration needs a certificate of insurance: $100,000 general liability, $300,000 bodily injury and $50,000 property damage, plus $500,000 of workers' compensation coverage if the contractor has employees.
The City plumbing contractor page lists no insurance amount.
City: a $20,000 performance bond payable to the City of Chicago, filed before the license is issued.
State: a $20,000 surety or indemnification bond, or a letter of credit for the same amount.
City plumber applicants pass a written exam and a practical exam, the written one first.
The State exam application asks for at least four years as an Illinois licensed apprentice plumber.
A plumber licensed by the City of Chicago can apply for a State plumber license without the State exam on this form.
A City plumbing contractor license runs one year. Contractors renew on the Department of Buildings web portal and mail proof of a current bond to Continental Testing Services.
State contractor registration expires September 30 each year.
A plumbing contractor registered with the State also needs a City of Chicago plumbing contractor license to work in Chicago.
State law lets a city of 500,000 or more people license its own plumbers, and a plumber licensed by such a city or by the State may do plumbing anywhere in Illinois.

trades.title: Chicago HVAC License: What the City Requires
trades.desc: No separate HVAC license on the Chicago pages we read: permit work needs a City general contractor, other work a home repair license, refrigerant EPA 608.
trades.card: General contractor or home repair license, EPA 608
trades.summary: No separate HVAC license on the City pages we read. Permitted HVAC work needs a City general contractor; refrigerant work needs EPA Section 608 certification.
trades.page_summary: The City pages name no separate HVAC or refrigeration contractor license. Here is which City license covers HVAC work with and without a permit, the stationary engineer license for boiler operators, and the federal refrigerant rule.

rows.text: The City has no separate HVAC or refrigeration contractor license on its permit pages. A permit to replace HVAC equipment, add a heat pump or air conditioning, or install refrigeration equipment needs a licensed general contractor, Class A to E by project cost. In some cases an owner who lives at the address may act as contractor with Form 401.

Home heating and cooling work such as central air, central heating, boilers, furnaces and hot water heaters falls under the City home repair license. If the work needs a building permit, a general contractor license is needed instead.
Running most steam and hot water boilers needs a City stationary engineer license for the person who operates them.
The State's list of licensed professions has no HVAC, heating, refrigeration or mechanical entry. No State agency page we read says the State licenses this work.
Where a City general contractor license is needed: $300 a year for Class E up to $2,000 a year for Class A, the same to renew.
Home repair license: $250, valid two years, and $250 to renew. BACP has also posted a business license fee update dated Jan 27, 2026 that we could not open, so ask BACP for the current fee.
Stationary engineer: $70 per exam, $30 for the 2 year license and $30 to renew.
Where a City general contractor license is needed: $1 million per occurrence for Class E up to $5 million per occurrence for Class A.
Home repair license: commercial general liability of at least $300,000 per occurrence.
The general contractor page lists no bond.
The general contractor page lists no exam.
Stationary engineers pass a written exam given by Continental Testing Services, are at least 20 and have 2 years of practical experience.
A general contractor license runs one year from issuance.
A stationary engineer license runs two years.
Not stated. The City trade license pages do not say whether a license from a suburb or another town counts in Chicago.

Technicians who maintain, service, repair or dispose of equipment that could release refrigerant need EPA Section 608 certification (Type I, II, III or Universal) from an EPA approved certifying organization. The certification does not expire.

trades.page_summary: The State of Illinois licenses roofing contractors. Here is the State license, its bond, insurance and exam, and what Chicago adds on the roof permit.

rows.text: A Chicago permit for roof repair (up to 25% of the roof), recover or replacement needs a licensed City general contractor, Class A to E by project cost, and the contractor or subcontractor doing the roofing holds a valid Illinois roofing contractor license.
Roof work on a home that needs no building permit falls under the City home repair license.

The Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation licenses roofing contractors. A limited license covers residential roofing on properties of 8 units or less; an unlimited license covers residential, commercial and industrial roofing. Every license needs a qualifying party.
State: $125 to apply for a limited or unlimited license; renewal is $62.50 a year.
Where a City general contractor license is needed: $300 a year for Class E up to $2,000 a year for Class A, the same to renew.

State: at least $250,000 per occurrence of property damage coverage and $500,000 per occurrence of liability coverage for bodily injury, plus proof of workers' compensation if the business has employees.
Where a City general contractor license is needed: $1 million per occurrence for Class E up to $5 million per occurrence for Class A.
State: $10,000 for a limited license and $25,000 for an unlimited license.
The qualifying party passes the residential exam (limited) or the residential, commercial and industrial exam (unlimited). The exam fee is $226, paid to Continental Testing Services.
State roofing licenses expire December 31 of each odd-numbered year, whatever the issue date.
Under State roofing law, a city, village or county that requires a building permit may not issue one to a roofer without proof of a current State roofing license.
The City roofing permit page does not mention licenses from suburbs.

General use work needs the General Standards exam; restricted use work adds one or more subcategory exams, such as termites, fumigation, or insects and rodents.

rows.text: The license table of the City's Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) lists a Private Scavenger license and a Junk Peddler license, both regulated business licenses. No City page we read says which one a home junk removal company needs.

BACP's junk peddler fact sheet says the license covers anyone who uses a vehicle to collect, dispose of or transport junk, including junk bought from people who want it hauled away.

Under the City recycling ordinance, every private hauler offers recycling, takes recyclables to a permitted facility, keeps a working GPS device on each vehicle and files a yearly report by February 28. A private scavenger license is not renewed if that report is late or incomplete.
On covered construction and demolition projects, at least 50% of the debris is recycled, and the waste hauler certifies that it was.
Illinois EPA requires a special waste hauling permit to haul special waste.

The State rule's definition of industrial process waste leaves out household waste, landscape waste and construction or demolition debris. The State pages we read list no license for hauling ordinary household junk.

Private Scavenger $250 and Junk Peddler $250, in a column headed per 2 years, as the BACP license table read on Oct 27, 2026. BACP has also posted a business license fee update dated Jan 27, 2026 that we could not open, so ask BACP for the current fee.

trades.card: City permit for sandblasting, grinding and chemical washing
trades.summary: The City's surface cleaning permit covers sandblasting, grinding and chemical washing. The City pages we read do not mention power or pressure washing.
trades.page_summary: Chicago's Department of Public Health permits sandblasting, grinding and chemical washing of building surfaces. Here is that permit, its fee, what the pages say and do not say about pressure washing, and the lead rules.

rows.text: The Chicago Department of Public Health requires an Architectural Surface Cleaning Permit for sandblasting, grinding or chemical washing of a building, statue or other architectural surface. Work cannot start until it is issued, and a copy stays at the job site.
The permit form lists three methods, dry grinding, dry sandblasting and wet chemical wash, requires notice to occupants of surrounding buildings, and treats painted surfaces as containing lead paint.

No City page we read names a license for this trade. The license table of the Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) lists a Limited Business license for general retail sales and services, says a business may need more than one license, and gives 312-74-GOBIZ as the number to call to find out which license applies.
BACP says it decides the license type from the business's activities.
BACP says most business activities in Chicago require a City business license.
The State's list of regulated professions has no pressure washing entry.
For lead paint work, Illinois EPA says high or low pressure washing needs all liquid waste contained and collected for proper disposal.
Surface cleaning permit: $150 per building or structure for the first calendar month and $100 for each month after.

Limited Business License: $250, issued for two years, as the BACP page read on Oct 27, 2026. BACP has also posted a business license fee update dated Jan 27, 2026 that we could not open, so ask BACP for the current fee.
The surface cleaning permit form lists no insurance amount.
The surface cleaning permit page lists no bond.
The permit form lists no exam. It asks whether paint samples were taken by a lead inspector licensed by the State of Illinois.
The permit page lists no renewal; the fee runs by the calendar month, $100 for each month or part of one after the first.
A Limited Business License is issued for two years and renewed before it expires.
Not stated. The BACP pages do not say whether a license from a suburb counts in Chicago.

EPA says pressure washing is not a prohibited practice under its lead-safe (RRP) rule and is subject to the same containment requirements, so no dust or debris, including in the waste water, leaves the work area. EPA points to the local water treatment authority about disposing of waste water.

trades.name: Snow removal
trades.title: Chicago Snow Removal Business License Rules
trades.desc: What a Chicago snow plowing or shoveling business needs: what BACP says about the City license, the City sidewalk clearing rules and fines, from agency pages.
trades.card: City business license, City sidewalk rules
trades.summary: No City or State page we read names a snow removal license. The City sidewalk rules set the path width and clearing times.
trades.page_summary: Snow plowing and shoveling have no license of their own on the City or State pages we read. Here is what the City says about a business license, and the City sidewalk snow rules for property owners.

rows.text: No City page we read names a license for this trade. The license table of the Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) lists a Limited Business license for general retail sales and services, says a business may need more than one license, and gives 312-74-GOBIZ as the number to call to find out which license applies.
BACP says it decides the license type from the business's activities.
BACP says most business activities in Chicago require a City business license.

City sidewalk rules: a cleared path at least 5 feet wide. Snow that falls 7 am to 7 pm is cleared by 10 pm, and snow that falls 7 pm to 7 am by 10 am. Snow may not be shoveled into the right-of-way, such as bus stops, parking spaces and bike lanes.
The State's list of regulated professions has no snow removal entry.

Limited Business License: $250, issued for two years, as the BACP page read on Oct 27, 2026. BACP has also posted a business license fee update dated Jan 27, 2026 that we could not open, so ask BACP for the current fee.
Fines for not clearing a sidewalk run $50 to $500, set by an Administrative Hearings judge.
The City license page we read lists no insurance amount.
The City license page we read lists no bond.
The City license pages we read list no exam.
A Limited Business License is issued for two years and renewed before it expires.
Not stated. The BACP pages do not say whether a license from a suburb counts in Chicago.
